title: Sentinel BI tokenflow readiness discovery
next_steps: Redwood to share streaming token/sec benchmark template and instructions
Customer to provide representative prompt set and 90/95/99 p95 target profiles
Schedule on-prem pilot feasibility call (private deployment) next week
Send SOC2 + ISO docs and draft network architecture for VPC option
action_items: Marco Chen: produce initial token/sec streaming benchmark run and upload results (due: 2027-09-15)
Maya Lopez: compile list of compliance questions and data residency constraints (due: 2027-09-13)
Lena Ortiz: send pricing sketch and Dedicated sizing options with burst plan (due: 2027-09-10)
summary: Discovery with Sentinel BI focused on p95 streaming latency targets, burst concurrency, and decision between Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Customer is sensitive to data residency and wants quantifiable token/sec benchmarks against their prompt mix. Action: Redwood to run benchmarks and share security artifacts; schedule pilot feasibility for private deployment.
topics: hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs
security: SOC2, KMS, VPC, audit logs
transcript:
[00:00] Lena Ortiz: Hi everyone, thanks for taking the time. Quick roll call?
[00:05] Rajiv Menon: Rajiv here.
[00:06] Aisha Rahman: Aisha, hi.
[00:08] Daniel Park: Daniel, SRE. Maya on security but she will join in a sec.
[00:12] Lena Ortiz: Great. Marco and Priya from Redwood are on too. We planned to talk through your latency/throughput goals and the hosted/dedicated/private tradeoffs. Sound good?
[00:19] Rajiv Menon: Yeah, we have pretty strict p95 targets for streaming - aim is under 160ms for short-turn chats and for longer generation we want steady token/sec throughput.
[00:27] Marco Chen: Okay, useful. Is that 160ms p95 for the end-to-end response or per-token streaming latency?
[00:33] Aisha Rahman: It's end-to-end for the user-facing chat UI. We do progressive rendering, so the per-token stream matters too - we need first-byte under 100ms ideally so the UI doesn't feel laggy.
[00:43] Priya Kulkarni: Helpful, thanks. What model family are you planning to run in production? That impacts kernel selection and batching.
[00:49] Aisha Rahman: Right now we prototype on a 13B open model and a distilled 7B for cheaper routes. We might move to a quantized 34B in fall for answers that need more context.
[01:00] Daniel Park: Also, we have bursts—embedding generation spikes when daily reports refresh. Typical baseline concurrency ~30, burst to 350 concurrent streams for 5 to 20 minutes.
[01:10] Marco Chen: That's a big burst factor. Are those concurrent streams short-lived (few tokens) or long-running generations?
[01:16] Daniel Park: Mix. For embeddings it's small token count but many parallel requests; for chat it's medium length, 150-400 tokens.
[01:23] Lena Ortiz: Understood. Two immediate routes: Hosted API with autoscaling and hot-pools for bursts, or Dedicated reserved capacity which you can size for baseline and add burst capacity; Private lets you keep data in VPC/onprem but changes the operational model.
[01:36] Rajiv Menon: Can you give more concrete numbers? For example, using a 13B quantized variant, tokens/sec per GPU and p95 with streaming?
[01:44] Marco Chen: Sure, rough numbers: on an A10-class GPU we typically see around 12-18 tokens/sec for 13B in float16 for step-wise generation; with our continuous batching and prefix caching that can go up to mid-20s tokens/sec for short sequences. But streaming per-token latency depends a lot on batch windows and network hop.
[02:02] Priya Kulkarni: Also worth noting that quantization to 4-bit changes the kernel mix and we see token/sec increase but sometimes p95 gets worse if KV cache handling isn't tuned.
[02:12] Aisha Rahman: That KV cache comment worries me—our chat frequently does multi-turn with large context. We need consistent p95 not just average.
[02:20] Marco Chen: Absolutely. We do KV cache evictions carefully and have tuning knobs—cache shard size, prefetching heuristics. For multi-turn with long context, Dedicated or Private tends to give more consistent p95 because you avoid noisy neighbors.
[02:33] Maya Lopez: Sorry for delay, I'm Maya. From security, we need to know: do you support KMS integration and can customer-managed keys be enforced? Also, audit logs and SSO via SAML.
[02:42] Priya Kulkarni: Yes on both. Private has the most control—BYOK + HSM path, VPC peering, private endpoints. Hosted supports customer KMS in many cases and detailed audit logs, but enterprise contracts are needed for full retention.
[02:55] Lena Ortiz: Quick question—what are your tolerances on tail latency during burst? Is 99th percentile going to be a dealbreaker?
[03:03] Rajiv Menon: 99th under 800ms for interactive chat is our red line, but we'd prefer 99th below 500ms. Above that users notice.
[03:11] Daniel Park: And for batch embedding jobs, throughput matters more than p95. We do nightly jobs that need to finish in windows.
[03:18] Marco Chen: Makes sense. For embeddings we recommend Dedicated pools you can reserve GPUs for the batch window; then route real-time chat to a different pool. Redwood's routing can split by route and model.
[03:27] Aisha Rahman: How do you handle sudden spikes? Suppose we have 300 concurrent short chats—do you have cold-starts for additional GPUs?
[03:34] Marco Chen: There is a cold start penalty to spin up new instances, typically 30-90s depending on image/distro and model size. For predictable bursts we advise reserving burst capacity or using warm pools. For true sporadic spikes, Hosted will scale but may impact p95 during the ramp.
[03:47] Lena Ortiz: We can also pre-warm using synthetic traffic during expected windows. Does Sentinel have any regulated time windows we can coordinate?
[03:54] Rajiv Menon: Yes, the end of quarter reports at 2am UTC, those spikes are predictable.
[03:58] Marco Chen: Great candidate for scheduled warm pools. We can include automated pre-warm runbooks in the Dedicated proposal.
[04:04] Maya Lopez: About encryption—data in transit and at rest must be AES-256; logs must be shippable to our SIEM and redact PII. Also, any model snapshots used for fine-tuning must stay in our VPC.
[04:15] Priya Kulkarni: Private deployment supports all of that. Hosted can support log forwarding and retention policies in enterprise tier; we'll share the specifics.
[04:22] Lena Ortiz: Back to performance—what's your target tokens/sec when you say 150-400 token responses?
[04:29] Aisha Rahman: For chat we want to sustain around 80 tokens/sec aggregate across the pool so that even during small burst windows the UI stream remains snappy. Per-request, per-connection rate should be high enough to stream new tokens every ~40-60ms ideally, but we know that's ambitious; p95 under 160ms first-byte is the measurable target.
[04:50] Marco Chen: Per-token every 40-60ms is very tight—depends heavily on network RTT and model compute. We can approximate: if per-token compute is 20ms and network RTT is 20-30ms you might get into that window, but for larger models compute dominates. For a 13B on modern accelerator, achieving 40ms per token is unlikely. We should instrument a benchmark with your exact prompt lengths.
[05:08] Daniel Park: Can you run that benchmark for us, with our prompt set?
[05:11] Marco Chen: Yes, if you provide the prompts and sample conversation traces we'll run a token/sec + p95 streaming run against hosted and a simulated Dedicated profile.
[05:20] Lena Ortiz: We'll also provide example config for prefetch and batch windows so you can see tradeoffs: aggressive batching improves throughput but increases first-byte latency.
[05:28] Rajiv Menon: What about cost? If we reserve Dedicated capacity for baseline and add burst keep a 20% overprovision for safety, what does that look like?
[05:36] Lena Ortiz: We'll sketch a few scenarios: pure Hosted with autoscale, Dedicated baseline sized for concurrency 30 and burst pool for +320, and Private—where you pay infra + support. We'll send a side-by-side cost per 1M tokens as well.
[05:48] Maya Lopez: Also include expected time to recover from node failure and how failover works between regions. We need SLA details.
[05:55] Priya Kulkarni: Our Dedicated SLA includes replacement and automated fallback to standby variants; cross-region failover is supported but adds latency. We'll include MTTR numbers in the pack.
[06:04] Daniel Park: On observability, can we get token-level cost attribution and traces showing where latency happened (network vs runtime vs batching)?
[06:12] Marco Chen: Yes, Redwood Console provides per-token breakdown, route-level traces, and flamegraphs for kernel time. We'll demo that in the next call.
[06:19] Aisha Rahman: Good. A few gotchas: our UI expects streaming chunk framing every ~80ms. If your stream bundling delays chunks, we need a fallback to short-poll.
[06:29] Marco Chen: We have stream chunk size config and you can set a max-latency flush. We'll show config.
[06:35] Lena Ortiz: Any competitors you're evaluating?
[06:37] Rajiv Menon: We're looking at CloudAI Endpoints for simplicity and LocalServe because they do on-prem. ModelHub Enterprise is in the mix because of price.
[06:45] Lena Ortiz: Noted. We'll address comparisons in the follow-up doc.
[06:49] Daniel Park: One more technical—how do you handle KV cache for multi-tenant setups? We don't want cross-tenant leakage or performance interference.
[06:56] Marco Chen: KV cache is partitioned per model instance; Dedicated gives dedicated GPU pools and stronger isolation. For Hosted we use tenant-aware sharding and quotas; we'll share the cache eviction heuristics doc.
[07:08] Maya Lopez: Please include certification levels for Private release; we have regulatory customers asking for on-prem options with no external egress.
[07:15] Priya Kulkarni: We have an on-prem package that runs without outbound telemetry by request, and we can sign addendums.
[07:20] Rajiv Menon: Ok recap from our side: we want the benchmark run, price sketches, security pack, and a pilot plan for private deployment feasibility.
[07:29] Lena Ortiz: Agreed. Marco will run benchmarks; I'll send pricing; Priya will assemble the pilot checklist.
[07:34] Marco Chen: I'll need prompt set, average context lengths, and a list of peak windows.
[07:39] Daniel Park: We'll deliver those by Monday.
[07:41] Lena Ortiz: Perfect. Any final off-the-record notes?
[07:43] Maya Lopez: Just that retention windows for logs must be configurable per dataset - we'll put details in the doc.
[07:48] Lena Ortiz: Thanks everyone, we'll circulate the follow-ups and target the pilot call for next Wednesday.
[07:54] Rajiv Menon: Thanks, bye.
[07:56] Aisha Rahman: Thanks.
[07:58] (call ends)
